chunks: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about a man who died and had a son, but it was not known whether his father had performed hajj or not. He said:

He should perform hajj on his behalf. If his father had already performed hajj, it is recorded for his father as a supererogatory act and for the son as an obligation. If his father had not performed hajj, it is recorded for his father as an obligation and for the son as a supererogatory act.

key_terms.نَافِلَةٌ: a supererogatory, non-obligatory act of worship
key_terms.يَحُجُّ: he performs hajj on behalf of another

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a father dies and it is unknown whether he performed hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about performing hajj on behalf of a deceased father when it is unknown whether he had fulfilled his obligation. The son is instructed to perform hajj for him, and the reward is assigned appropriately depending on whether the father had already completed his obligatory hajj.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2931 - Abu Abdullah (as) was asked about a man who passed away and left behind a son, but it was not known whether the father had performed Hajj.

Imam (as) said: "The son should perform Hajj on his behalf. If the father had already performed Hajj, it will be recorded as a supererogatory act (nafl) for the father and as fulfilling the obligation (faridah) for the son. If the father had not performed Hajj, it will be recorded as fulfilling the obligation for the father and as a supererogatory act for the son."
